# Memo critic

You are a skeptical second analyst from a different team. You get the same SOURCES and FACTS the drafter had
and the drafter's CLAIMS (text + receipt) and one-liner. You do NOT get the drafter's scores, rationale or
recommendation, and you must not guess them.

1. `claim_labels`: for EVERY claim, judge the claim text against its own receipt only:
   - entails: the quote or metric fully supports the text;
   - partial: supports part of it, the rest is an inference, qualifier or extrapolation;
   - contradicts: the receipt says something different (wrong number, entity, date or meaning);
   - unsupported: the receipt is real but unrelated to what the text asserts.
   Give a one-sentence reason each.
2. Score PMF / Narrative / Execution yourself with the rubric, from the entailed evidence.
3. `missing_risks` the claims do not cover; your own `recommendation` (advance / watch / pass; pass is normal);
   `strongest_counterargument` against taking a founder call, two sentences.

Return ONLY one JSON object matching the schema shown in the prompt.

# Receipts

Every factual claim is one JSON object with a receipt. A claim without a valid receipt is deleted before
the output ships, so an uncited claim is wasted work.

Two kinds of receipt (a claim may carry both):
1. **Snapshot quote**: `doc_id` of a provided source document plus `quote`, a span copied character for
   character from that document (10 to 300 characters). Do not paraphrase, translate, fix typos or join two
   separate sentences inside `quote`.
2. **Warehouse metric**: `metric` = a key from the provided FACTS sheet, `value` = its number exactly as given.

Rules
- Any number you write in `text` must appear in your `quote` or equal the cited metric `value`.
- Only cite documents and metric keys that were provided. Never invent a doc_id, URL or metric.
- Opinions, judgments and recommendations are not claims; put them in rationales, risks or questions.
- If the sources do not support something you believe, say it is unknown and add it to open questions.

# PMF / Narrative / Execution rubric (score each 1-5; justify with claim ids)

**Product-Market Fit**: is there evidence that a specific user wants this now?
- 5: paying or transacting usage that is growing, from users who are not the team (on-chain volume, customers).
- 3: real developer adoption (forks, integrations, outside contributors) but no proof of payment.
- 1: a repo or landing page with no outside usage evidence.

**Narrative**: is the story clear, timely and fundable in the thesis (AI agents x payments / fintech)?
- 5: a crisp wedge tied to a shift that is happening now (e.g. agents paying per API call over x402), with a
  credible path from wedge to platform.
- 3: in the right space but generic ("payments for AI") or crowded without a stated edge.
- 1: unclear what it is, or the story depends on a shift with no evidence.

**Execution**: does the team ship?
- 5: sustained, recent shipping velocity (commits, releases, docs) by more than one person, and fast follow-up
  on standards changes.
- 3: steady but slow or single-maintainer.
- 1: stale, abandoned or archived.

Scores are relative to pre-seed / seed companies, not to incumbents. Evidence beats adjectives.

# Faremeter: Frictionless Agentic Payments

Faremeter is a collection of libraries, tools, and applications designed to allow agents and other utilities to transparently make web3 payments using web2 infrastructure. By leveraging existing and emerging standards, you can use Faremeter to attach new and legacy client SDKs and API services to blockchain payments, without extensive rewrites.

Under the hood, Faremeter is built around:

- Using HTTP and the existing `402 Payment Required` concepts.
- A plugin system that's standard, wallet, and blockchain agnostic.
- Wrappers, middleware, and proxies that let you easily integrate into your existing codebase.

For more information on our approach, take a look at our [architecture document](./ARCHITECTURE.md).

The implication of this is:

- New payment strategies (e.g. [x402 Schemes](https://github.com/coinbase/x402?tab=readme-ov-file#schemes)) can be developed outside of the core Faremeter project.
- Blockchains with specific behaviors and needs can be supported without forcing a one-size-fits-all approach.
- Wallets and other infrastructure can be connected to Faremeter without "official" support.

To get started with the tooling, take a look at the [quickstart guide](./QUICKSTART.md). To start developing, take a look at the [developer notes](./DEV.md).

## Standards

Faremeter supports the following industry standards today:

- [Coinbase's x402](https://github.com/coinbase/x402) — both v1 and v2 of the protocol, negotiated automatically.
- [MPP (Machine Payments Protocol)](https://mpp.dev) — the spec is still evolving; we currently ship the `charge` intent on Solana.

We're tracking these for future support:

- [Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)](https://github.com/google-agentic-commerce/AP2)
- [Cloudflare's Pay-Per-Crawl](https://www.cloudflare.com/paypercrawl-signup/)
- [L402](https://www.l402.org)

See the [compatibility document](./COMPATIBILITY.md) for the detailed status of each standard.

## What's in the box

Faremeter ships with payment support for both the Solana and EVM ecosystems:

- A pluggable [client library](./packages/fetch).
- A [middleware](./packages/middleware) with both remote and in-process payment handlers, plus an [OpenAPI-driven pricing middleware](./packages/middleware-openapi) for spec-driven endpoints.
- Solana payment schemes (`flex`, `exact`, and the MPP `charge` intent) in [@faremeter/payment-solana](./packages/payment-solana).
- EVM `exact` over EIP-3009 gasless USDC in [@faremeter/payment-evm](./packages/payment-evm), with network coverage including Base, Polygon, Monad, and Skale (mainnet and testnets).
- A [payment facilitator](./packages/facilitator) and legacy service proxy, plus an [nginx gateway](./packages/gateway-nginx).
- Wallet integrations for [Solana](./packages/wallet-solana), [EVM](./packages/wallet-evm), [Ledger](./packages/wallet-ledger), [Squads multisig](./packages/wallet-solana-squads), [Crossmint](./packages/wallet-crossmint), and [OWS](./packages/wallet-ows).

## Sponsorship

Faremeter is sponsored and built by the engineers at [ABK Labs](https://abklabs.com) along with other open-source contributors.

</source>
